Because `package.json`'s `bin` field points straight at `./dist/cli.js` and consumers install this via npm/npx (including as a global CLI), the package can't rely on TypeScript, tsx, or other devDependencies being present at install time — pre-building and committing `dist/` guarantees the CLI runs immediately after `npm install` with no compile step. The only script that does compile (`compile`) is wired to run at publish time via `prepublishOnly`, not at install time, which is exactly why no install-time lifecycle hook exists in this repo.

SCRIPTS: preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare

The safeguard is `isProjectPath` in `src/core/manifest.ts` (manifest.ts:42-46).

`readManifest` (same file, line 64-67) filters every manifest entry through `isProjectPath(cwd, entry.path)` before returning the file list. Any entry whose `path` is absolute, drive-qualified (`C:\...`), or resolves outside `cwd` via `..` gets dropped there — so `sync.ts`'s deletion loop (`src/commands/sync.ts:128-141`, which calls `path.join(cwd, p)` then `rmSync`) never even sees an entry like `../secret.txt`; it's already gone from the manifest by the time `readManifest` returns it.

Concretely, `isProjectPath` rejects a path if:
- it's not a non-empty string,
- `path.isAbsolute(p)` is true, or
- it matches a Windows drive prefix (`^[a-zA-Z]:`), or
- resolving it against `cwd` produces a relative path that starts with `..`.

So editing the manifest's `files` list to add `../secret.txt` or `C:\secret.txt` doesn't work — that entry is stripped before `sync` ever iterates over it for deletion.

## Summary

Fixed `backupPath()` in `src/commands/sync.ts:38-43`: it previously always returned `<file>.bak`, so a second forced sync clobbered the backup of the original hand-written file. It now checks if `.bak` exists and, if so, finds the next free `.bak.N` suffix, preserving every prior backup.

Added a regression test in `tests/regressions.test.ts` verifying that three successive forced syncs with hand-edits in between produce `CLAUDE.md.bak`, `CLAUDE.md.bak.1`, and `CLAUDE.md.bak.2`, each retaining its own distinct content.
